doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Views on today's music, The Beatles and fusion
summary: Wilder does not condemn younger musicians, recalling that he first thought The Beatles were terrible but came to respect them.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you think of the state of music these days? How’s that for an open question?

No, not really. It’s strange and there are a lot of things that of course the younger musicians have different ideas about how the music should be played and the kind of music. And I don’t condemn them for it, I guess because of the era in which I grew up, I don’t relate to it too well, but I remember a time when I thought The Beatles were terrible when they first — I thought it was some of the worst garbage I’d ever heard. But as I began hearing more and more of it I began to acquire a great respect for what they were doing, and a lot of what they did was tremendous and has influenced a lot of the things that we do today and that are acceptable. So I won’t put down any of the young people, the young guys with the rock, or what do they call it, “third stream” and —

Fusion and those things. I mean it’s just another aspect of music. And I’m sure that as time goes on there’ll be other developments that come along. But from those there will be a lot of well established styles that will be accepted.
